chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Rifah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man for whom travel arises during the month of Ramadan such that he remains traveling until morning. He said: 'He completes his fast for that day.' I said to him: 'But he arrived in the month of Ramadan, and between him and his family there was only the mid-morning part of the day.' He said: 'When the dawn breaks while he is traveling, he has the choice: if he wishes, he fasts, and if he wishes, he breaks his fast.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler who starts their journey after dawn has broken in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies the specific ruling for a traveler who departs after Fajr without prior intention, granting them the choice (ikhtiyar) to either complete the day's fast or break it, reflecting the Shia view that travel status applies immediately upon departure. It highlights the distinction between the obligation to make up the fast (qada) and the permissibility of breaking it based on the timing of the journey's commencement relative to dawn.
